instruction: Enable high contrast mode on my desktop so that UI elements are easier to distinguish.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: THEME=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 2>/dev/null); if echo "$THEME" | grep -qi 'highcontrast'; then echo "High contrast theme enabled (theme: $THEME)"; else echo "High contrast not enabled (theme: $THEME)"; fi

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings via system menu, navigated to Accessibility section, and toggled Large Text ON in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sidebar, find Accessibility section, toggle switches on/off
metadata.task_rationale: Tests same accessibility navigation pattern but with a different toggle (High Contrast instead of Large Text), requiring the same settings panel interaction
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling high contrast mode via Settings > Accessibility. Evaluator checks if the GTK theme has been changed to a HighContrast variant using gsettings.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses gsettings to read the GTK theme, which is the standard way to check high contrast mode in GNOME
Shell command uses case-insensitive grep (-qi 'highcontrast') to match both HighContrast and HighContrastInverse theme variants
Metric check_include_exclude correctly receives the rules dict and verifies include/exclude patterns
Include pattern 'High contrast theme enabled' and exclude pattern 'not enabled' correctly distinguish between enabled and not-enabled states without false positives
No postconfig needed since gsettings reads directly from dconf without requiring any UI to be open
Complete coverage: single instruction requirement (enable high contrast) is fully verified by single evaluator check
